newsitem.title: UK: Modern Panamaxes help steady dry cargo freight.
newsitem.headline: Modern Panamaxes help steady dry cargo freight.

text.p: A disappointing month for owners which started with the Baltic Freight Index at 1516 has at least ended more positively - the index today recorded its first gain for nearly 3 weeks, up 6 points to 1367.
Caper rates have been softer throughout this week, but owners' brokers remain optimistic that this situation will be reversed next month, especially in the Atlantic.
Meanwhile the situation for Panamaxes has already been to some extent reversed, in particular for modern types in the Atlantic.
Owners' brokers report grain rates rising on voyage basis and timecharter. It is also believed by many brokers that handy-size grain levels may have bottomed out in the atlantic.

GRAIN - Charterers have been introducing Feb/March enquiries into the market. South Koreans have been more active in the US Gulf/Far East trades and there is reported to be a much more positive tone for Panamaxes in general.
Grain operators on Brazil and Argentina have appeared as charterers for tonnage for short period business and the number of orders for Handies and Panamaxes from this area has increased.

Grain fixtures reported included Theogennitor 116,978 dwt delivery US Gulf early Feb trip Saudi Arabia at $9,500 daily plus $225,000 bonus by Geepee, but owner's brokers denied the report, possibly because the vessel failed on subjects.

Cargill were rumoured to be working the 1974-built Cornilios 64,000 dwt for prompt heavyrain US Gulf/Continent at a firmer level approaching $12.00. On timecharter the 1981-built Menites 64,896 dwt was understood fixed on subjects by Korea Line delivery US Gulf mid Feb trip far East (possibly Thailand) at close to $12,500 daily plus $250,000 bonus.

Rumours circulated that the 1994-built Hai Ji 70,083 dwt was fixed on subjects by Hanjin US Gulf/far East at between $13,750-14,000 daily plus about $275,000-300,000 bonus, and that the 1995-built Konstantinos a 71,550 dwt had fixed and failed on subjects for similar business at $14,500 daily plus $320,000 bonus.

The difference in rates obtainable by such modern tonnage and older Panamaxes was well illustrated by Keoyang's reported fixture of the 1981-built Atlantic Sovereign 65,015 dwt delivery US Gulf about Feb 10 trip far East at $11,000 daily plus $200,000 bonus.
Elsewhere Noble fixed Ikan Beliak 64,957 dwt delivery E.C. Australia Feb 15/25 trip with grain to Bin Qasim at a modest $8,500 daily plus $125,000 bonus.

There was generally more activity in the handy-size category in Atlantic grain. Continental booked Catherine for 30,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Morocco spot/prompt at $16.00, and Andre fixed 25,000 wheat Tilbury/Poland for Jan/Feb at $8.25.
MINERALS etc the 1975-built Derby North 64,000 dwt was reported fixed by Italian charterers delivery prompt Med for a transatlantic round at $7,750 daily.
The 1989-built Achilles 68,779 dwt was understood booked by NYK delivery Hongkong for a coal trip via Indonesia to Japan at under $10,000 daily.

HANDY-SIZES - Rates continued firm for large modern craned tonnage on the Continent. A 43,000 dwt vessel was rumoured fixed from the Continent to the far East at $12,500 daily, but a similar vessel was understood to have received under $11,500 daily from the Black Sea to the same destination.
